reasons: No tests are visible for this file.
The backend folder can carry a secret key file into the shared zip.
Old build folders are deleted without asking.

terms.meaning: a folder that runs without being installed
a Windows script file that runs a list of commands in order
a settings file that PyInstaller writes for a build

depends_on: QUICK_START.md, RUNNING_GUIDE.md and SETUP_INSTRUCTIONS.md (copied if present)

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and setup
sections.what: Brings in the file and folder tools the build needs. Nothing runs here.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: print_step
sections.title: Console heading helper
sections.what: Prints a framed heading so each build step is easy to spot in the console output.
sections.why: Likely reason: makes long console output easier to follow. Reason not stated.

sections.name: check_pyinstaller
sections.title: PyInstaller availability check
sections.what: Checks that PyInstaller can be imported. If it cannot, installs it with pip and carries on.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets someone run the script without preparing the tools first. Reason not stated.
sections.watch_out: The check tests the Python running this script, but the build later runs a separate pyinstaller command, which may come from a different install.

sections.name: clean_build_dirs
sections.title: Old build cleanup
sections.what: Deletes the old build, dist and portable folders and the old spec file, so each build starts clean.
sections.why: Likely reason: stops old and new files from mixing. Reason not stated.
sections.watch_out: Anything saved inside those folders is lost without any confirmation.

sections.name: build_executable
sections.title: Program file build
sections.what: Runs the PyInstaller command that packs launcher.py into one program file, bundling the backend, the interface file, the environment template and some libraries. An error here stops the build.
sections.why: Likely reason: one file is easy to hand to teammates. The code comment on the one-file option supports this.
sections.watch_out: The bundling entries use a semicolon, the Windows form, while build_exe.py uses a colon, so the two scripts disagree.

sections.name: create_portable_package
sections.title: Portable folder assembly
sections.what: Creates the UniversalRAG-Portable folder and copies in the program file, the full backend folder, the interface file, the environment template and any existing guides. It then writes the start guide and the batch file.
sections.why: Likely reason: gathers everything teammates need into one folder. Reason not stated.
sections.watch_out: Copying the whole backend folder can also copy a backend .env file that holds a real API key.

sections.name: create_team_readme (part 1)
sections.title: Start guide opening sections
sections.what: Builds the first part of the plain-text start guide: what the app does, the first-time setup, and the daily use steps.
sections.why: Likely reason: teammates may not know Python, so the guide uses plain language. The wording of the guide shows this.
sections.watch_out: The guide text lives inside this code, so any change to the app needs a matching edit here.

sections.name: create_team_readme (part 2)
sections.title: Start guide examples and troubleshooting
sections.what: Adds example questions, a troubleshooting list and pointers to the longer guides.
sections.why: Likely reason: common problems are answered in advance. Reason not stated.
sections.watch_out: The troubleshooting messages describe error text that may change when the app changes.

sections.name: create_team_readme (part 3)
sections.title: Start guide cost and closing sections
sections.what: Adds the cost notes, help links and closing lines, then writes the complete guide to README_START_HERE.txt.
sections.why: Likely reason: sets expectations about cost and says where to get help. The text shows this purpose.
sections.watch_out: Cost figures are fixed numbers in the text and will go stale as prices change.

sections.name: create_batch_launcher
sections.title: Batch file fallback launcher
sections.what: Writes LAUNCH_ALTERNATE.bat, a backup way to start the app that checks for Python and then runs launcher.py.
sections.why: Likely reason: a second start method in case the program file fails. The batch file's own text says this.
sections.watch_out: The batch file needs Python installed on the teammate's computer, which the portable package does not include.

sections.name: create_zip
sections.title: Zip creation
sections.what: Zips the portable folder into UniversalRAG-Portable-v1.0.zip and prints its size, or prints the error if zipping fails.
sections.why: Likely reason: a single file is easy to send. Reason not stated.
sections.watch_out: The version name is typed in, so it must be changed by hand for each new release.

sections.name: main
sections.title: Full build sequence
sections.what: Runs the whole build in order and prints the sharing instructions. It stops and reports the first failure it meets.
sections.why: Likely reason: each step depends on the one before, so a failure should stop the rest. Reason not stated.
sections.watch_out: The result of the zip step is ignored, so the success message can print even when zipping failed.

sections.name: entry point
sections.title: Script entry point
sections.what: Runs the build when the file is started directly and sets the exit result to success or failure.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets other tools read whether the build worked. Reason not stated.

summary: Builds a Windows portable folder and zip for teammates, containing the program file, backend, a plain-text start guide and a batch launcher.
purpose: Packages the app so teammates can run it without seeing any code.
why: Stated in the docstring: it creates a distributable package for teammates.
how: The script first checks that PyInstaller is available and installs it if not. It deletes old build folders and the old spec file. It runs PyInstaller on the launcher, bundling the backend, the interface file and the environment template. It then makes a portable folder holding the program, the backend, the interface file, the template, any existing guides, a plain-text start guide and a batch launcher. The folder is zipped and instructions are printed. The script pauses for Enter at the beginning.
inputs: The project files in the current folder: launcher.py, simple_ui.html, .env.template, the backend folder, and optional guide files.
outputs: A UniversalRAG-Portable folder, a UniversalRAG-Portable-v1.0.zip file, a dist folder holding the program file, and printed instructions.
risks: The whole backend folder is copied, so any .env file inside it would be shipped in the zip with its secret key. Old build folders are deleted without asking. The version number is typed in by hand. A failed zip is printed but does not stop the script. The Enter pause means the script cannot run unattended. The start guide includes cost figures that will go out of date.
debug: If the program file is not found, read the PyInstaller output above the error. If the zip is missing, read the error line near the end. Before sharing, check the portable folder for any .env file inside the backend folder.
